feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is stated for it. Iteration 1 (score 337.6) established that the ±0.03 m array gave line_loss_events of 1.0 per run on s-bend and slalom, with max_error about 0.06 on both, and iteration 0 with ±0.04 m gave the same loss of 1.0 per run. So the line is lost at the array edge on bends in both designs. In iteration 1, narrowing the track and raising the wheel radius moved oval finishes from 3 to 17 of 20 but left s-bend progress flat at about 0.24 (iteration 0 was 0.24). That suggests turn authority is not the only limit. For the next race: if line_loss_events on s-bend and slalom fall to 0 and max_error drops below about 0.05, keep the ±0.06 m span and try a modest wider or narrower span. If line_loss_events stay at 1.0 on bends but max_error stays at about 0.06, the limit is authority and the wheel track should narrow. If oscillation rises sharply, pull the row back toward y=0.06, as the Integrator will do if needed.
requested_changes: Keep the 7-sensor span at ±0.06 m with 0.02 m pitch at y=0.07 if line_loss_events on s-bend and slalom fall below 1.0 per run. This is supported by iteration 1 (±0.03 m gave 1.0 per run) and iteration 0 (±0.04 m gave 1.0 per run).

If max_error on s-bend and slalom stays near 0.06 with no change in progress, narrow wheel_track from 0.10 to 0.09 m. Iteration 1 showed that narrowing the track did not change s-bend progress (0.24 both times), so try this step only if the span change alone does not help.

If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.3 on the oval (iteration 1 was 0.20), move the sensor row back from y=0.07 to y=0.06 m. Iteration 0 at y=0.06 had oscillation of 0.32 on the oval, so the forward row is the more likely fix to try, not the widest span.
